source_review.notes: Checked current Linux documentation for network scaling, NAPI, socket buffers, checksum and segmentation offloads, network-device features, XDP metadata, page pools, AF_XDP and ethtool netlink. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; kernel contracts, driver/device requirements, abstract queue models, operational guidance and assurance remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked packet layout, header geometry, checksum, segmentation, feature, queue, indirection, NUMA, execution, ownership and reference notation.
Reviewed logical segment counts, RSS selection, multidimensional queue load, remap ordering and final feature intersection.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates deferred wire work, logical packet units, placement generations, resource ownership and final-path capability.

evidence: Executed replacement of an eight-bucket RSS table after queue 2 failure.
Confirmed exactly two buckets move, six stay stable, affected hashes 2 and 6 remap, and unaffected hash 7 remains on queue 3.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates one abstract indirection replacement only; it implements no NIC, hash, queue drain, flow ordering, driver or packet.

evidence: Re-derived logical segment count from payload and segment size and RSS queue selection from hash and indirection table.
Checked strict-order handoff across old/new backlogs and intersection of device, route, packet, protocol and policy features.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are subsystem reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of Linux networking, device offload, RSS, DMA or ordering.

evidence: Reviewed plain and nested tunnels, fragments, NAT, GSO limits, checksum levels, feature withdrawal, malformed metadata and unsupported devices.
Reviewed hash collisions, queue failure, backlogged remap, CPU hotplug, NUMA mismatch, XDP redirect, AF_XDP teardown, DMA reset and page-pool references.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Geometry, offload, hash, queue, ordering, ownership, capacity, reconfiguration, reset and observation boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced checksum, segmentation, aggregation, RSS, RPS, RFS, XPS, interrupts, NAPI, NUMA, XDP, AF_XDP and reconfiguration.
Verified exact metadata, final feature eligibility, software fallback, compatible aggregation, live queue graphs, ordered handoff and one recycle path.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats bytes, offload metadata, device features, queues, CPUs, pools, userspace rings and generations as coupled but independently owned state.

evidence: Reviewed checksum states, GSO/TSO/USO, GRO/LRO, logical accounting, RSS, RPS/RFS/XPS, affinity, NUMA, XDP/AF_XDP, fallback and reset.
Constructed counterexamples for flag-as-completion, SKB-as-wire-packet, advertised-feature-as-eligibility, balanced-interrupts-as-balanced-work and remap-as-performance-only.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable offload and scaling obligations, not a formal proof of Linux, a driver, NIC, firmware, DMA platform, topology or workload.

evidence: Audited uses of checksummed, segmented, aggregated, hashed, queued, steered, polled, redirected, completed, recycled, remapped and reset.
Confirmed kernel rules, device requirements, abstract models, recommendations, tests and assurance claims remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Deferred checksum is not labeled completed checksum, aggregate is not labeled wire packet, configured affinity is not labeled actual execution and device completion is not labeled peer delivery.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-079/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for the RSS indirection replacement model.
Reviewed required kernel, driver, firmware, device, feature, queue, CPU, NUMA, traffic, fault, capture and receiver evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes one abstract mapping only; it provides no evidence for NIC programming, flow ordering, offload correctness, DMA lifetime, wire bytes or performance.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed offload as deferred wire-correctness metadata and receive scaling as an ordering-aware live queue-placement graph with explicit software fallback.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed current mechanisms as implementable concerns, including checksum levels, tunnel segmentation, aggregation compatibility, RSS/RPS/RFS/XPS, XDP, AF_XDP, page pools, hotplug and reset. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from offload contracts and logical units through RSS and software steering, queue/CPU/NUMA topology, XDP ownership, reconfiguration, fallback and testing, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, Linux networking maintainer, network-driver or NIC-vendor, performance, security, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
